summary: Clarified CloudTrail's default event history, current Health naming, EventBridge, and X-Ray instrumentation lifecycle.

changes.find: - The CloudWatch Events name will be replaced with EventBridge
changes.replace: - CloudWatch Events is the earlier name for these event-bus capabilities. Use Amazon EventBridge terminology; EventBridge Scheduler is a separate scheduling capability.

changes.find: - CloudTrail is enabled by default!
changes.replace: - CloudTrail event history is available by default for the last 90 days of management events in each Region. This is not a trail that automatically retains every API/data event indefinitely.

changes.find:
- Events are stored for 90 days in CloudTrail
- To keep events beyond this period, log them to S3 and use Athena
changes.replace:
- Event history covers 90 days of management events. Data events require configuration and are not included in event history.
- Configure a trail to S3 for longer retention and select the event types required for the audit. S3 data can be queried with Athena. CloudTrail Lake has separate availability and retention rules; it is not a new-customer default.

changes.find: - Helps analyze and debug distributed applications by providing request tracing.
changes.replace: - Helps analyze and debug distributed applications by providing request tracing. The X-Ray service remains available, but the X-Ray SDKs and daemon entered maintenance on 25 February 2026. Prefer supported OpenTelemetry instrumentation for new work.

changes.find: - Uses machine learning to identify:
changes.replace:
- CodeGuru Reviewer no longer accepts new repository associations; existing associations can continue. Its following capabilities describe existing-customer/historical use, not a recommendation to onboard a new account:
- Uses machine learning to identify:

changes.find: ## AWS Status - Service Health Dashboard
changes.replace:
## AWS Status - Service Health Dashboard

Current name: the public service-health view of AWS Health Dashboard. Use [health.aws.amazon.com](https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/status).

changes.find: ## AWS Personal Health Dashboard
changes.replace:
## AWS Personal Health Dashboard

Current name: the account-health view of AWS Health Dashboard. Public service status and account-specific events are different views of AWS Health.

summary: Corrected Inspector scope, root-only tasks, KMS terminology and rotation, ACM certificate pricing, and several overly broad security claims.

sources.title: Security Hub CSPM and AWS Config

changes.find: - Ensure AWS employees can’t access your data
changes.replace: - Operate the service infrastructure with AWS access-control and data-protection controls; customers still configure who may access their data.

changes.find: - Enabling encryption for objects (e.g., server-side or client-side encryption).
changes.replace: - Select suitable encryption and access policies. New S3 uploads are already encrypted with at least SSE-S3; stronger or client-side requirements remain a customer design decision.

changes.find: - Prevents DDOS attack
changes.replace: - Helps detect and mitigate DDoS attacks; do not interpret protection as a guarantee that every attack is prevented.

changes.find: - 24/7 access to AWS DDoS response team (DRP)
changes.replace: - Shield Advanced includes eligibility for Shield Response Team assistance; expert response and cost-protection features are not blanket Shield Standard benefits.

changes.find: - AWS customers are welcome to carry out security assessments or penetration tests against their AWS infrastructure without prior approval for 8 services:
changes.replace: - AWS permits testing customer-owned resources on its current permitted-services list without prior approval, subject to the penetration-testing policy. The following examples are not an exhaustive or permanently fixed list:

changes.find: - Encryption Opt-in:
changes.replace: - Encryption configuration depends on the service; do not assume all entries below are unencrypted by default:

changes.find: - S3 buckets: Server-side encryption of objects
changes.replace: - S3: all new uploads have default SSE-S3 encryption; optionally select other supported modes.

changes.find: ## Types of Customer Master Keys: CMK
changes.replace:
## Types of Customer Master Keys: CMK

Current terminology is **KMS keys**. CMK is the older name. Distinguish customer managed keys, AWS managed keys, and AWS owned keys.

changes.find: - Possibility of rotation policy (new key generated every year, old key preserved)
changes.replace: - Eligible customer managed symmetric keys support configurable automatic rotation periods (90 to 2,560 days), with 365 days as the default, and on-demand rotation. Rotating key material does not change the key ID; previous material remains available to decrypt older ciphertext.

changes.find: - Free of charge for public TLS certificates
changes.replace: - Non-exportable public certificates used with integrated services have no ACM certificate charge. Exportable public certificates and private CA services have charges; not every ACM certificate is free.

changes.find: - Remember: only for EC2 instances and container infrastructure
changes.replace: - Inspector scans supported EC2 workloads, ECR container images, and Lambda functions. Supported scan modes and resource coverage vary; Inspector Classic is a retired, separate service.

changes.find: - Amazon Macie is a fully managed data security and data privacy service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and protect your sensitive data in AWS.
changes.replace: - Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data and evaluates security/privacy risks in supported S3 data. It does not automatically scan all databases or all data in every AWS service.

changes.find: - Must first enable the AWS Config Service
changes.replace: - Security Hub CSPM controls that use AWS Config require the relevant Config recorder and resource recording. This is not a prerequisite for every Security Hub finding integration or every newer Security Hub capability.

changes.start: - Lock away your AWS account root user access keys!
changes.replace:
- Do not create root access keys. Protect root sign-in with MFA and use federated workforce access for routine work.
- Do not memorize the old claim that changing a support plan is root-only: authorized IAM principals can change plans. Organizations can also centrally perform some privileged tasks for member accounts.
- Tasks that still require root credentials in the applicable account context include changing the root password and configuring S3 MFA Delete. Account closure and recovery have standalone/member-account distinctions; consult the current task list rather than assuming root is always the only path.

[AWS root-user guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_root-user.html) and [support-plan changes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/changing-support-plans.html) explain the exceptions.

changes.find: - Inspector: For EC2 only, install agent and find vulnerabilities
changes.replace: - Inspector: vulnerability assessment for supported EC2, ECR, and Lambda resources; scan modes vary.

changes.find: - Change or cancel your AWS Support plan
changes.replace: - Check the current task-specific permissions; changing support plans can be delegated to authorized IAM principals.

summary: Removed unsupported accuracy/cost promises, clarified SageMaker AI and Bedrock, and identified restricted Forecast and Kendra services.

changes.find: - No upfront payments, 80% cheaper than traditional contact centers
changes.replace: - Pricing depends on channels, features, and usage. An advertised comparison does not guarantee an 80% saving for every contact center.

changes.find: - Organizes text files by topic
changes.replace: - Core text-analysis features include entities, key phrases, and sentiment. Topic modeling, event detection, and prompt-safety classification have separate availability restrictions; do not assume all historical features are open to new customers.

changes.find: ## Amazon SageMaker
changes.replace:
## Amazon SageMaker

The model-building service is now called **Amazon SageMaker AI**. The broader SageMaker product family includes additional data and AI capabilities. **Amazon Bedrock** provides access to foundation models for generative AI applications; distinguish this from building and training your own models.

changes.find: - Fully managed service that uses ML to deliver highly accurate forecasts
changes.replace: - Historical/existing-customer forecasting service. Amazon Forecast has been closed to new customers since 29 July 2024. For new workloads, evaluate the supported forecasting tools named in AWS's migration guidance.

changes.find: - 50% more accurate than looking at the data itself
changes.replace: - Forecast accuracy depends on data and evaluation; there is no general 50% accuracy guarantee.

changes.find: - Fully managed document search service powered by ML
changes.replace: - Managed enterprise document search service. Kendra is closed to new customers under its current availability notice; distinguish its historical capabilities from a recommendation to onboard a new account.

changes.find: - **Forecast**: Accurate forecasts
changes.replace: - **Forecast**: existing-customer forecasting service, closed to new customers.

changes.find: - **Kendra**: ML-powered search engine
changes.replace: - **Kendra**: enterprise search with new-customer restrictions.

summary: Clarified public/private subnet routing, Direct Connect encryption, endpoint support, VPN termination, and deployment-dependent NAT behavior.

changes.find:
- A public subnet is a subnet that is accessible from the internet
- A private subnet is a subnet that is not accessible from the internet
changes.replace:
- A public subnet has a direct route to an internet gateway. Internet reachability also requires suitable addressing and security rules.
- A private subnet has no direct route to an internet gateway; it can still use configured egress or private connectivity.

changes.find: - Allows instances in the VPC to directly communicate with the internet.
changes.replace: - Provides an internet path when routing, public IPv4 or IPv6 addressing, and security rules permit it. Attaching an internet gateway alone does not make every instance public.

changes.find: - Managed by AWS
changes.replace: - Managed by AWS. This outbound-internet example describes a public NAT gateway; private NAT gateways serve different connectivity use cases. Match NAT deployment and resilience to the current zonal or regional offering.

changes.find: - VPC Endpoint Interface: the rest
changes.replace: - Interface endpoints: supported AWS and other PrivateLink endpoint services, not automatically every AWS service. Check service and Region support.

changes.find: - AWS: must use a Virtual Private Gateway (VGW)
changes.replace: - AWS termination can use a virtual private gateway or transit gateway, according to the supported VPN architecture.

changes.find: - The connection is private, secure and fast
changes.replace: - Provides dedicated connectivity. Direct Connect traffic is not encrypted by default; use an appropriate VPN, supported MACsec, or application encryption when required.

changes.find: - Takes at least a month to establish
changes.replace: - Provisioning time depends on the connection, provider, facility, and existing connectivity; there is no universal one-month minimum.
